newsitem.title: CHINA: Taiwan firm wins first trademark case in China.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan firm wins first trademark case in China.

text.p: China has ruled in favour of a Taiwan company in a dispute over the use of a trademark in the first case of its kind involving Chinese and Taiwan companies, the Wen Hui Bao newspaper said on Wednesday.

The trademark appraisal committee of the State Industrial and Commercial Administration Management Bureau ruled that the Qijia Chemical Company of Putian, Fujian province, could not use the "Xiebao" trademark and that this trademark belonged to the Taiwan Xiebao Enterprise Shareholding Co, it said.
The Taiwan company registered the trademark, for a resin used in making shoes, in Taiwan in 1984 and started to sell the product in China in 1988, it said.
In 1992, the Taiwan company set up a joint venture in the southern city of Zhanjiang, using the trademark, it said.
In August 1994, a Hong Kong businessman who had set up a factory in Putian to make shoe resin registered the "Xiebao" trademark with China's State Trademark Bureau, it said.

In September 1995, Taiwan Xiebao applied to the State Trademark Bureau to cancel the registration of the Putian factory and the bureau recently ruled in its favour, ordering the Putian plant to stop using the trademark, it said.
It did not give any more details.
